textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 6 maths · Lines and Angles · Textbook Concepts
textbookBox.concept: A point is a precise location. It has no length, breadth or height. The tip of a sharpened pencil or a needle gives an idea of a point, and we name points with capital letters like Z, P and T.

1.tip: Look closely at the diagram on the board as we explain each property.

beats.en: A point is a precise location. It has no length, breadth or height. The tip of a sharpened pencil or a needle gives an idea of a point, and we name points with capital letters like Z, P and T.
beats.speakEn: A point is a precise location. It has no length, breadth or height. The tip of a sharpened pencil or a needle gives an idea of a point, and we name points with capital letters like Z, P and T.

beats.en: An angle is formed by two rays with a common starting point. The common starting point is the vertex and the two rays are the arms. For rays BD and BE with vertex B, we write angle DBE or angle EBD, using the symbol ∠.
beats.speakEn: An angle is formed by two rays with a common starting point. The common starting point is the vertex and the two rays are the arms. For rays BD and BE with vertex B, we write angle DBE or angle EBD, using the symbol ∠.

type: Key Concept: A point is a precise location. It has no length, breadth or height.
Rule: An angle is formed by two rays with a common starting point.

textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 6 maths · Lines and Angles · Deeper Textbook Ideas
textbookBox.concept: To compare two angles, trace one and place it over the other so that the vertices coincide and one arm lies on the same line. This is called superimposition.

beats.en: To compare two angles, trace one and place it over the other so that the vertices coincide and one arm lies on the same line. This is called superimposition. The angle whose second arm lies outside is the larger one.
beats.speakEn: To compare two angles, trace one and place it over the other so that the vertices coincide and one arm lies on the same line. This is called superimposition. The angle whose second arm lies outside is the larger one.

beats.en: Turn the book cover through a half turn so it lies flat. The two arms now lie on one straight line, and the angle is called a straight angle. Fold the paper so one arm falls on the other arm.
beats.speakEn: Turn the book cover through a half turn so it lies flat. The two arms now lie on one straight line, and the angle is called a straight angle. Fold the paper so one arm falls on the other arm.

textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 6 maths · Lines and Angles · Complete Summary
textbookBox.concept: To give an angle a number, mathematicians divided the angle at the centre of a circle into 360 equal parts. The size of each part is 1 degree, written 1°.
